children: AtkinsRealis and partner Aecon landed a three-year, 1.7 billion Canadian dollars (US$1.2 billion) deal for the refurbishment of a unit at the Pickering nuclear power station in Ontario.

AtkinsRealis's Candu Energy business in a joint venture with Aecon signed the contract with Ontario Power Generation to begin Unit 5 work associated with the Pickering Nuclear Generating Station's retube, feeder and boiler replacement project.
The contract represents the first retube, feeder and boiler replacement unit in a broader refurbishment project, with similar work expected on Units 6, 7 and 8 in subsequent phases.

The work covers engineering and design services, project delivery, and program and project management associated with the planned life-extension of four of Pickering's Candu reactors, including work that would enable Unit 5 to operate until the 2060s, AtkinsRealis said.
AtkinsRealis said its share of the contract will be added to its nuclear backlog in the third quarter.
Candu is a registered trademark of the federal government's Atomic Energy of Canada that is used under exclusive license by AtkinsRealis's  Candu Energy subsidiary.
